indicators.name: Fed Net Liquidity
indicators.formula: net liquidity = Fed total assets − Treasury general account − reverse repo. Scored on the percentile rank of its 20-week change within its own trailing 120, inverted so rapid expansion reads calm.
indicators.flag: Replaces four indicators (Fed Balance Sheet, Bank Reserves, TGA, Liquidity Flow Stress) that read the same balance sheet twice over.
steps: pool = the last 120 such changes, ranging -569,840 to 363,711

indicators.name: Treasury Vol Proxy (MOVE-style)
indicators.source_note: synthetic proxy from 2Y/10Y 5-day moves — the real MOVE index isn’t freely available via FRED
indicators.formula: clamp((|2Y 5-day move in bps| × 0.6 + |10Y 5-day move in bps| × 0.4) × 2, 0, 100)

indicators.name: Real 10-Year Yield
indicators.formula: Percentile rank of the 10-year TIPS yield within its own trailing 1000 observations.
indicators.flag: New. Replaces the separately-weighted nominal 2Y and 10Y, which were each also counted inside the Treasury Vol Proxy.
steps: pool = last 1000 observations of DFII10, ranging 1.06 to 2.68
997 of those 1000 sit below the current 2.61

indicators.name: Yield Curve (10Y − 3M)
indicators.formula: clamp(50 − 25 × (10Y − 3M), 0, 100). Reads 50 at a flat curve and rises as it inverts.
indicators.flag: Replaces 2s10s, which carried 0% weight because it was the difference of two already-scored yields. 10Y−3M is a distinct series with the stronger recession record.

indicators.name: Market Volatility
indicators.flag: Merges the old VIX and VIX Momentum rows, which read the same series and together carried 10%.
steps: momentum: VIX 14.81 vs 15.84 five sessions ago = -6.50%

indicators.name: Equity Breadth
indicators.source_note: live via SPY/RSP — unavailable in the original workbook
indicators.formula: clamp(50 − (5-day RSP-vs-SPY spread × 12 + 20-day spread × 7), 0, 100). Equal-weight lagging cap-weight means a narrow market.
indicators.flag: Merges S&P 500 Breadth and Market Participation Momentum, which used these same two spreads and correlated at 0.989.
steps: RSP vs SPY over 5 sessions = -2.615%  (equal-weight minus cap-weight)

indicators.name: Financial Conditions (NFCI)
indicators.formula: Percentile rank of the 20-observation change within its own trailing 500 — fast tightening scores high.

inputs.label: Chicago Fed National Financial Conditions Index

steps: pool = the last 500 such changes, ranging -0.81 to 0.88

indicators.name: Jobless Claims Momentum
indicators.formula: clamp(50 + (initial claims 5-week % change) × 5, 0, 100). Reads 50 when claims are flat.
indicators.flag: Renamed from “Economic Surprise”. A surprise index measures data against consensus forecasts; this measures claims against their own recent level, so the old name overstated it.

indicators.name: Inflation Momentum
indicators.formula: clamp(50 + ((core CPI m/m × 0.35 + core PCE m/m × 0.35 + trimmed-mean PCE m/m × 0.30) − 0.2) × 200, 0, 100). Reads 50 at 0.2% monthly, roughly the 2% annual target. Falls back to a 50/50 CPI-PCE blend if the trimmed mean is unavailable.
indicators.flag: Renamed from “Inflation & Labor Momentum”. No labour series ever fed it. Now blends the Dallas Fed trimmed mean, which drops the biggest movers in each tail every month instead of always removing food and energy.
steps: core CPI 337.765 vs 336.789 last month = 0.290% m/m
core PCE 130.658 vs 130.338 last month = 0.246% m/m

asset_outlook.note: Regime-conditioned historical tendencies from the source workbook, not guaranteed forecasts. "Relative UP" means the asset may still decline but has often held up better than broad equities.

real_yields_note: Ex-post real yield = long-term government bond yield minus year-over-year CPI. This is inflation that has already happened, not the market-priced expectation a US TIPS yield (DFII10) represents, so it is not the same quantity as the Real 10-Year Yield indicator above. Sources are OECD series via FRED, published monthly with roughly a month’s lag — useful for the structural picture across countries, not for timing. Currency moves are 60 business days, shown as the foreign currency’s gain against the dollar.

spread.label: A2/P2 − AA, 30-day
spread.description: What a lower-rated non-financial borrower pays over the best-rated one for the same money at the same tenor — the standard commercial-paper credit-stress gauge.

bill_spread.label: CP − T-bill, 90-day
bill_spread.description: AA nonfinancial paper over the 3-month Treasury bill: the premium for unsecured corporate funding against the risk-free alternative at the same tenor.

commercial_paper.note: Commercial paper rates from the Federal Reserve via FRED, quoted on a discount basis. The release is posted once daily at about 1pm ET, so this panel changes once a day even though the rest of the page refreshes every 15 minutes — “live” here means the latest published day, not intraday. On days when trade volume is too thin to support a calculation the Fed publishes no rate at all; those gaps are carried forward on the chart, and every row shows its own last real observation date so a stale leg stays visible. Monitoring only: this panel is not scored into the Overall Risk number above.

price_history_note: Daily closing prices and a daily-resolution reconstruction of the risk scores, both refreshed on this 15-minute schedule. Each asset is charted against a risk sub-metric grouping — but a rigorous out-of-sample test (train/test split, no regime bucket, one metric tested per asset independently) found a real, holding-up relationship for only 1 of 22 assets: Short Treasuries / T-Bills vs. Fed Balance Sheet (marked with a ✓ badge below). Every other pairing here is an illustrative grouping, not a validated predictor. "Real-time" here means "as of the latest 15-minute refresh, using the latest available daily close" — not intraday tick data.
